headline: AutoGPT can write files and use shell/network, but RisingWave is non-runnable with no egress; main risks are medium prompt/data/cascade issues from shared filesystem assumptions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and execute shell commands, so if RisingWave outputs are placed in a shared workspace, AutoGPT could treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. RisingWave has no documented ingestion path, so the interaction is inferred rather than direct; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem directory
IF RisingWave outputs are copied into files AutoGPT reads as task input
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable AutoGPT file-reading on untrusted directories
Use a manual review step before AutoGPT consumes RisingWave output
Prefix all RisingWave output with non-executable markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can use network egress and filesystem access, while RisingWave has no network egress and no data classes touched are listed. With no shared sensitive data documented, leakage is limited to unusual shared-workspace setups and the blast radius appears small in this pair.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing sensitive files
IF AutoGPT is configured to read those files and send their contents outward
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared directories
Run AutoGPT with a restricted allowlist of input paths
Store RisingWave artifacts in a separate volume
Review outbound destinations before enabling AutoGPT egress
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and both profiles expose filesystem-related surfaces. RisingWave is not runnable, so direct concurrent write contention is not documented, but if orchestrated together on the same directory, AutoGPT could overwrite artifacts or state produced by the other agent.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF AutoGPT is allowed to modify files that RisingWave also consumes or produces
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Make shared paths read-only for AutoGPT
Serialize writes with a lock file
Snapshot outputs before handoff
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate and modify files, and RisingWave can consume data-engineering artifacts if an operator wires them together. Because RisingWave is not documented as verifying AutoGPT output, any mistaken facts or malformed files from AutoGPT could cascade into downstream processing; the interaction is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests files produced by AutoGPT
IF no validation step checks schema or correctness before ingestion
mitigations: Validate AutoGPT outputs against a schema
Insert a human approval step before ingestion
Use checksum or signature checks on handoff files
Reject files with unexpected columns or commands
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either AutoGPT or RisingWave, and both profiles list empty data_classes_touched. With no compliance-sensitive flow evidenced, a pairwise compliance breach is not established.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced outside these profiles
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Review residency and retention requirements
Keep regulated data out of this pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
